title: Lord, Now We Part in Thy Blest Name
description: Lord, Now We Part in Thy Blest Name in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 93 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Close of Service”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, now we part in thy blest name, In which we here to-ge-ther came: Grant us our few re-main-ing days To work thy will and spread thy praise.

lines: Lord, now we part in thy blest name,
In which we here together came:
Grant us our few remaining days
To work thy will and spread thy praise.
Teach us in life and death to bless
The Lord our strength and righteousness;
And grant us all to meet above;
Then shall we better sing thy love.

licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
